quotes.text: Transaction limits: Minimum amount: 1.00 MYR (B2C), 2.00 MYR (B2B); Maximum amount: 30,000.00 MYR (B2C), 1,000,000.00 MYR (B2B)
You can issue a full or partial refund for an FPX payment within 180 days of the original payment
FPX supports iOS and Android Payment Sheet for B2C transactions only.
A B2C payment immediately displays as successful. A B2B payment initially displays as pending while confirmation is processed asynchronously, then displays as successful after confirmation.
To reconcile an FPX payment with PayNet records, retrieve the PaymentIntent with `latest_charge` expanded and read `latest_charge.payment_method_details.fpx.transaction_id`.

old_evidence.text: FPX payments can be refunded up to 60 days after the original payment.
Refunds for FPX payments are asynchronous and take approximately 1 week to complete.

findings: The new capture identifies FPX as a single-use Malaysian bank redirect for MY customers/MYR, domestic use, MY merchants/platforms, with BRN required to process payments and receive payouts. It states no recurring, setup_future_usage, SetupIntent, off-session, manual capture, or standard chargeback process. Up to T+5 payout timing is distinct from immediate payment confirmation and provisional access (new raw lines 9-65, 80-110; old raw lines 8-71; source lines 13-22).

The consequential refund change is old 60-day submission and about one week completion versus new 180-day submission, normally up to 14 days and possibly six weeks. The new refund is full/partial, asynchronous, noncancelable after submission, and a separate credit rather than a card-like reversal. Use Refund status or refund.updated/refund.failed for final outcome; a failed refund returns funds to Stripe balance and requires an alternative customer refund (old raw lines 36-38, 117-119; new raw lines 57-78; source lines 13, 20).

The new capture adds B2C 1-30,000 MYR and B2B 2-1,000,000 MYR transaction bounds, B2C-only iOS/Android Payment Sheet, and a confirmation distinction: B2C immediately displays successful, while B2B initially displays pending until asynchronous confirmation. Browser return after authorization is a navigation state, not an independently verified payment success (new raw lines 36-40, 112-141; old raw lines 73-93; source line 24).

The new product table says Billing and Invoicing supported but footnotes send_invoice collection only, while recurring, SetupIntents and off-session payments are unsupported. This must not become an automatic subscription or charge_automatically claim. The older capture explicitly excluded Checkout setup/subscription mode; keep that dated, and scope the new Billing row to its footnote (old raw lines 62-71; new raw lines 86-115; wiki/concepts/stripe-bank-redirects.md lines 29-34).

The new overview adds statement descriptor semantics and FPX PayNet reconciliation ID: full statement_descriptor controls seller order number, card-only suffix does not; Connect direct/on_behalf_of uses connected-account descriptor, destination without on_behalf_of uses platform. Read the PaymentIntent latest_charge.payment_method_details.fpx.transaction_id for PayNet reconciliation, not a generic returned-page state (new raw lines 143-151).

Older source/concept details about mandatory confirmation-page fields, separate FPX balance/payout routing and bank lists come from the separate accept-payment guide, not the new overview. Preserve those as dated route-specific authority rather than deleting them because absent here (wiki/concepts/stripe-fpx.md lines 45-53; wiki/stripe-index.md line 278).
substantive_changes: Refund submission 60 to 180 days, processing approximately one week to normally up to 14 days/potential six weeks, noncancelability and credit/Refund status detail (old raw lines 117-119; new raw lines 57-78).
New B2B/B2C payment limits and display/confirmation-state split, plus B2C-only native Payment Sheet boundary (new raw lines 36-40, 112-141).
New account eligibility, product/API support, send_invoice qualifier, statement descriptor routing and PayNet transaction_id locator (new raw lines 16-40, 86-115, 143-151).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the 2026-05-03 capture's 60-day/~one-week refund statement and optional merchant return dated; the 2026-11-07 overview differs and must be named explicitly (old raw lines 73-93, 117-119; new raw lines 68-78, 135-141).

Retain BRN, MY/MYR, bank authentication/redirect, no recurring/disputes and T+5 payout as continuing facts; preserve older historical PayNet/BNM and 2018 transaction-count prose as historical rather than assuming the new shorter wording disproves it (old raw lines 8-54; new raw lines 9-42).
conflicts: Current source and FPX concept state 60-day/~one-week refund behavior (source lines 13, 20; wiki/concepts/stripe-fpx.md lines 30, 41-42), while the new capture states 180 days, normally up to 14 days and possibly six weeks (new raw lines 57-78). Add reciprocal dated warnings and update comparison row.

The current source/concept describes an optional merchant return after completion (source line 24; wiki/concepts/stripe-fpx.md lines 18-23), whereas the new overview says customer automatically returns and B2B initially displays pending (new raw lines 135-141). Preserve the older flow as dated and avoid implying return is payment success.

The FPX concept says legacy Elements min RM2/max RM30,000 (wiki/concepts/stripe-fpx.md line 53), but the new overview gives B2C 1/30,000 MYR and B2B 2/1,000,000 MYR (new raw line 40). Treat legacy UI and B2B/B2C scope separately, not an unconditional replacement.

The current source says Checkout subscription/setup unsupported (source line 22), old raw says the same (old raw line 71), while new product table's Billing support is send_invoice-only and its SetupIntent/off-session entries are negative (new raw lines 96-115). This is a qualified product-row difference, not support for automatic recurring.
unresolved_questions: The overview does not confirm an individual merchant's BRN, capability activation, bank availability, or runtime success; the pending B2B display and merchant return are not settlement or funds-availability proof (new raw lines 18-24, 121-141).

The linked accept-payment guide, not this overview, is needed to reconcile exact mandatory confirmation-page fields and historical legacy-Elements limits with current UI variants (new raw lines 112-157; wiki/concepts/stripe-fpx.md lines 45-53).

findings: Add exact canonical URL and new pinned provenance, retain old raw, update refund window/timing/state and B2B/B2C amount/confirmation boundaries, plus send_invoice-only Billing and B2C-only mobile scope (source lines 1-28; old raw lines 117-119; new raw lines 36-40, 57-78, 86-115, 139-141).

Route to FPX concept for historical accept-payment guide facts; new overview's statement descriptor and PayNet transaction ID deserve locators rather than generic payment-success claims (new raw lines 143-151).

source_assessments.reason: The new capture materially changes refund operations and adds B2B/B2C payment limits and outcome distinctions missing from the existing source.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/fpx, the new capture establishes a single-use MY merchant/customer, MYR domestic bank redirect with required BRN for processing and payouts, no recurring or standard disputes, and T+5 settlement separate from confirmation (new raw lines 9-65, 80-110). It adds B2C 1-30,000 MYR and B2B 2-1,000,000 MYR limits, B2C-only native Payment Sheet, and B2B pending display before asynchronous confirmation; bank authorization and browser return do not prove settlement (new raw lines 36-40, 112-141). Refunds now have a 180-day submission window and normally up to 14 days, possibly six weeks, to complete; final Refund status matters (new raw lines 57-78). The matched old capture said 60 days/about one week (old raw lines 117-119), which source-stripe-fpx.md still repeats, and its optional-return flow also differs (source lines 13, 20, 24).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/fpx, substantive changes are the 60-to-180-day refund window, longer stated processing range and noncancelable separate-credit workflow, B2B/B2C limits and status split, B2C-only mobile sheet, send_invoice-only Billing qualifier, and descriptor/PayNet reconciliation fields (old raw lines 62-71, 73-93, 117-119; new raw lines 36-40, 57-78, 86-115, 135-151). source-stripe-fpx.md and the FPX concept must keep their 2026-05-03 refund/return statements dated with reciprocal warnings; the concept's legacy Elements amount limit is UI-specific. New headings, pricing/sample links and replacement of video/flow images with prose are presentation or navigation, not evidence those older references are deprecated. Billing support is not automatic recurring, a B2B pending display is not success, and neither browser return nor submitted refund proves final payment or refund outcome.
